key_insight: Sparse Autoencoder Geometric Anchoring (SAGA) reduces catastrophic forgetting by constraining representation drift along input-dependent, low-rank directions.
engineering_relevance: SAGA may help engineering AI models retain prior knowledge during sequential updates, though solid-mechanics applications were not evaluated.
method: Train a sparse autoencoder at each task boundary.
Use replay examples and leading encoder-Jacobian singular directions to anchor local representations.
Retain geometric constraints without keeping the autoencoder during subsequent training.
evidence_signal: On three pretrained ViT-B/16 Class-IL benchmarks, SAGA achieved the highest mean accuracy and lowest mean forgetting among evaluated baselines, with accuracy gains of 12.15, 4.79, and 3.22 percentage points on CIFAR-100, CUB-200, and ImageNet-R.
watch_item: Results from scratch were mixed, and implementation requires replay, snapshot history, and a choice of constraint rank.
paper_title: Sparse Autoencoders Can Induce Local Geometry for Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting
